narrative.title: Vending Combinations from Unlimited Coin Bins
narrative.scenario: A parts dispenser stocks bins of distinct bolt sizes, and maintenance orders can request any total length — with a bin reused as many times as needed. The dispatcher builds each order by walking the sorted bins: either draw from the current bin again (target shrinks, bin stays) or move on to the next bin for good. Every branch whose remaining target hits exactly zero is a valid fulfilment plan.
narrative.inputFormat: An array candidates of distinct positive integers and an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: Every combination summing to target, sorted lexicographically by the verifier.

complexity.optimalSpace: O(target) recursion depth beyond the output

testCases.explanation: Two plans: one bin of 7, or 2 drawn twice plus a 3.
Unlimited reuse means 2 can anchor a four-draw plan as well as pair with 3s.

hintLevels: Level 1: The only decision per step is which bin to draw next and whether to keep drawing from it.
Level 2: Recurse on (index, remaining): reuse means calling with the same index and remaining minus the bin's value; skipping means index + 1.
Level 3: Sorting the candidates lets each branch stop the moment a bin overshoots the remaining target — the pruning keeps the tree shallow.
